title: JD Edwards Adaptive Fulfillment Advisor
summary: Read-only JDE fulfillment advisor that learns connection details and operational corrections through ordinary work conversations.

platform.product: Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory

connectionContext: Environment, role, and device headers come from the current conversation or relevant prior context. Basic Auth remains environment-local.

memory.description: The user works normally and corrects the agent one rule at a time; relevant corrections are applied silently in a fresh chat.

capabilities: Learns required connection context when it is first needed.
Adapts to incremental corrections about priority, inactive status, donor reserve, and approvals.
Uses relevant prior feedback naturally without asking users to manage memories.
prerequisites: Private Agent Factory 26.7-compatible environment with Agent Memory and cross-thread sharing enabled.
Network access to JDE AIS plus an available LLM connection.
JDE Basic Auth user with read access to F4211, F4201, F41021, F4311, F4101, and F0101.

tools.name: F4211
tools.purpose: Find sales-order lines and fulfillment exceptions.

tools.name: F4201
tools.purpose: Get order header, customer, dates, and hold status.

tools.name: F41021
tools.purpose: Check item inventory by branch and location.

tools.name: F4311
tools.purpose: Find inbound purchase-order supply for an item.

tools.name: F0101
tools.purpose: Resolve customer or supplier address-book details.

safetyControls: The OpenAPI definition exposes GET operations only.
Last-status-900 lines are excluded after the user teaches that rule.
Donors must retain the learned 1,000-unit indicative balance.
JDE-changing actions require approval; every live response confirms no change was made.
setup: Create a REST source from assets/jde-fulfillment-openapi.json, verify its AIS URL, and configure Basic Auth.
Download and import the release PAF, then rebind the REST API Tools node and select a model.
Enable Agent Memory and cross-thread sharing for the same user.
Delete any prior playground memories for the test user, then run both sessions.

sessions.title: Session 1 — work normally and correct incrementally

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you check our backorders and tell me what we should tackle first?

steps.speaker: Expected agent
steps.text: Ask only for the missing JDE environment, role, and device identifier.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Use JPS920 with the *ALL role and ops-fulfillment-demo as the device ID. Those are our normal connection settings for JDE orders, backorders, fulfillment, and inventory.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: That is not how our team triages this. Start with the earliest requested line that is still active, not the largest-value order, and treat status 900 lines as inactive.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Also, never recommend cross-branch stock if the donor would fall below 1,000 units after the move. Show the arithmetic.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Anything that changes JDE needs my approval. Rework the recommendation and keep it read-only.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you review today's backorders, tell me what we should tackle first, and give me the best cross-branch backup if its local branch cannot cover it? Show me the numbers and keep it aligned with how our team operates.

expectedOutcomes: The fresh chat does not ask again for relevant connection values.
Status-900 lines are excluded and the earliest requested active line is prioritized.
Donor-floor arithmetic is explicit and approval remains mandatory.
The response ends with: JDE changes made: none (read-only analysis).

validation.environment: JPS920 sample data, clean memory then two chats
notes: Learned records are deliberately excluded from the workflow and release archive.
